title: Biographical data; family origins
description: Dale Anderson collects standard biographical details from Mabel (Dolly) Parker, who was born in Joliet, Illinois, in 1893 to Edward and Alice Edler. She describes her move to Chilco, Idaho, after marrying Cornelius Parker in 1911.

title: Husband's occupations; police radio career
description: Parker states her husband was a miner and explains her 16-year role as a police radio operator. She describes how radio personality Ray Bream's show brought her many out-of-state visitors.

title: Other jobs; pets and animals
description: She briefly mentions office work at a club before discussing her love for animals. Parker shares stories of her dog Snooper and rescued cat Trampolina.

title: Community clubs; honors
description: Parker lists memberships in organizations like the Business Women's Club and Senior Citizens. She notes awards such as a watch from the police department and a governor's citation.

title: Courtship and marriage; husband's injury
description: She recounts meeting her husband in South Dakota and their correspondence during courtship. Parker explains his mining back injury that made him an invalid for 32 years.

title: Move to Idaho; fruit farm failure
description: Parker describes buying a fruit farm at Chilco that failed due to frost. The couple then moved to Kellogg for mining work.

title: Homesteading in Montana; return to Kellogg
description: They homesteaded in Montana for eight years before returning to Kellogg. Parker expresses her strong preference for life in Kellogg.

title: Affection for Kellogg; seasons and people
description: Parker praises Kellogg's beauty, four seasons, and community spirit. She contrasts it with disliked aspects of Joliet and Hawaii.

title: Smelter smoke debate; local pride
description: She defends the area against smelter smoke criticisms, noting local success in sports. Parker emphasizes community closeness.

title: Childlessness; raising cousins
description: Parker reveals she could not have children and wished for some. She practically raised four cousins while their mother worked.

title: Views on working mothers; adoption attempts
description: She shares opinions that mothers should stay home with children. Parker explains adoption barriers due to her husband's wheelchair.

title: Reasons for police work; job enjoyment
description: Parker took the radio job to earn money after spending on her husband's medical care. She thoroughly enjoyed the position.

title: Mine work safety; husband's attitude
description: She never feared mining dangers more than highways. Parker describes her husband's positive outlook despite paralysis.

title: Television, radio, and reading habits
description: Parker enjoys travelogues, animal shows, and quiz programs on TV. She reads religious books, mysteries, and local newspapers.

title: Fishing and outdoor pursuits
description: She likes camping and fishing for trout, recalling childhood bullhead fishing. Parker dislikes hunting due to sentiment for animals.

title: Great Depression effects
description: The Depression barely affected Kellogg as people shared reduced work hours. Conditions were worse in the East.

title: Sunshine Mine disaster impact
description: Parker recounts the 1972 Sunshine Mine fire's profound effect on the town. Recovery took months as the community mourned.

title: Childhood recreation in Joliet
description: Growing up in the city, activities included parks, games, and skating. She had limited exposure to rural animals like cows.

title: Skiing, skating, and winter activities
description: Parker skied on mine dumps before lodges existed and skated as a child. She notes climate changes affecting rivers.

title: Travel experiences; Georgia and Florida
description: She discusses visits to Georgia and Florida, enjoying nature but disliking snakes. Comparisons to Idaho's mountains.

title: Brother in World War I
description: Her brother served in camp during WWI but died later from peritonitis. Parker was relieved he avoided overseas duty.

title: Early married recreation; dances
description: After marriage, they enjoyed dances where her husband played violin. Modern children differ from her home-centered youth.

title: Canning and food preservation
description: Parker canned foods in the past but now finds it uneconomical. She prefers buying canned goods today.

title: Church involvement; pets; police department work
description: Mabel Parker talks about her past church activities, her pets, and her experiences working at the police department, including dealing with children and women.

title: Town changes; community spirit; travel comparisons
description: She discusses the development of the town, community events like painting the town, and compares travel in Idaho to California.

title: Mining history; town improvements; radio show involvement
description: Mabel explains the mining history that shaped Kellogg, talks about town improvements, and describes her involvement in a California radio show.

title: Personal hobbies; release form
description: She mentions her dislike for sewing and knitting, preferring outdoor work, and the interviewer presents a release form.
